title: Where the Line Gives Way
statement: A city, a specimen, a witness, and a distant ground are arranged as instructions that cannot remain obedient. Their edges overlap until classification becomes interpretation: architecture grows, history leans, and the horizon becomes a stage for choosing what to follow.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent where following an instruction ends and interpreting it begins.

notes.note: Establishing a layered dialogue between civic architecture, botanical instruction, historical portraiture, and lunar distance; the composition will leave room for later interpretation through overlap and scale.

actions.title: Where the Line Gives Way
actions.statement: A city, a specimen, a witness, and a distant ground are arranged as instructions that cannot remain obedient. Their edges overlap until classification becomes interpretation: architecture grows, history leans, and the horizon becomes a stage for choosing what to follow.

notes.note: The first arrangement establishes a clear threshold at the lunar horizon, but the upper field is too quiet. I’m introducing two contrasting visual “instructions”—a commercial poster and a densely symbolic manuscript—so the empty space becomes an active zone where commands turn into competing interpretations.

The canvas now reads as a suspended field of competing directives, but the lunar ground is still too cleanly separated from the historical fragments. I’m adding the crowd in the surf as a transitional band: a collective movement that physically crosses the boundary between image, ground, and interpretation.

The latest canvas makes the threshold legible: the crowd now sits between the historical fragments and the lunar ground, while the botanical plate behaves like an imposed central diagram. I’m adding a small, frontal portrait as an observing interpreter and bringing the buried city forward so the work has a visible counter-instruction rather than only atmospheric overlap.

The final canvas is visually resolved: the botanical diagram and Flatiron form a central vertical instruction, while the poster, manuscript, flamingo, portraits, surf, and lunar ground pull that instruction into competing readings. The title and statement are present and nonblank.
